plan.title: bug: engine:_ts-build hasCmd uses sh/command -v and never sees Corepack on Windows native

narratives.Description: engine:_ts-build and pm-run detect tools with sh -c 'command -v', which always fails on Windows native when sh is missing from PATH. Corepack.cmd is present but never selected, so builds fail-close claiming Corepack is missing. Replace hasCmd with a cross-platform probe that uses shell:true --version (resolves .cmd/.exe), preserve #2411 step order (pnpm → corepack@pin → corepack → fail), and keep #2181 no-auto-build on session verbs.
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

#2410 / PR #2411 added a Corepack-aware package-manager resolver for `engine:_ts-build`, but tool detection still shells out to Unix `sh -c 'command -v <name>'`. On **Windows native** (PowerShell / go-task), `sh` is often **not** on PATH, so `hasCmd('pnpm')`, `hasCmd('corepack')`, and even `hasCmd('node')` all return false. The resolver then fail-closes with "neither pnpm nor corepack is available" even when `corepack.cmd` is present and `corepack prepare pnpm@… --activate` works from PowerShell.

This leaves maintainer `task policy:show` / any `_ts-build`-gated verb broken on Windows after the #2410 fix, while `task session:start` (global fallback, #2409) already works.

## Observed (Windows 11 native, directive master @ v0.73.1, 2026-07-09)

Environment:
- `node` v24.18.0, `npm` 11.16.0 present
- `corepack` → `C:\Program Files\nodejs\corepack.cmd` (0.35.0)
- `pnpm` **MISSING** on PATH (even after `corepack prepare pnpm@11.8.0 --activate`)
- `sh` **MISSING** on PATH
- `bash` present via WindowsApps; Git present
- Local `packages/cli/dist/bin.js` and `node_modules` absent (cold source tree)

Repro:
```
task policy:show
```

Actual:
```
deft: neither pnpm nor corepack is available to run "build".
  Enable Corepack for the pinned manager: corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@11.8.0 --activate
  Or set DEFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER=npm for an explicit npm build path.
task: Failed to run task "policy:show": … engine:_ts-build: exit status 127
```

Meanwhile from PowerShell:
```
corepack --version          # 0.35.0
corepack prepare pnpm@11.8.0 --activate   # succeeds
```

Node mimic of the shipped `hasCmd`:
```
pnpm false
corepack false
node false
npm false
```
because `execFileSync('sh', ['-c', 'command -v …'])` cannot start `sh`.

Contrast: `task session:start` exits 0 via global `deft` fallback (#2409/#2411). Global `deft policy:show` works after upgrading to `@deftai/directive@0.73.1` (#2367/#2412).

## Root cause

In `tasks/engine.yml` (both `pm-run` and the inlined `_ts-build` resolver), detection is:

```js
const hasCmd=(name)=>{
  try{
    execFileSync('sh',['-c','command -v '+name],{stdio:'ignore'});
    return true;
  }catch{
    return false;
  }
};
```

That assumes a POSIX `sh` with `command -v`. Windows Task/Git Bash environments often lack a bare `sh` on PATH, so the Corepack steps are never queued even though `corepack.cmd` exists.

`trySteps` never runs Corepack; the function jumps straight to the exit-127 remediation that tells the operator to enable Corepack — which they already have.

## Expected

- Detect `corepack` / `pnpm` / `npm` on Windows without requiring Unix `sh`
- Prefer PATH lookup that understands `.cmd` / `.exe` shims (e.g. `where`, `shell: true` with `corepack --version`, or Node's own resolution)
- With Corepack present and `packageManager: pnpm@…` pinned, `_ts-build` should invoke Corepack (or succeed via `DEFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER=npm`) instead of falsely claiming Corepack is missing
- Remediation text should only claim Corepack is missing when it actually is

## Proposed approach

1. Replace `sh`/`command -v` detection with a cross-platform probe (try `execFileSync(name, ['--version'], {shell: true})` or `where`/`where.exe` on win32).
2. Keep the existing step order: bare `pnpm` → `corepack pnpm@<pin>` → `corepack pnpm` → actionable fail.
3. Add a Windows-native contract/regression test that mocks `sh` absent + `corepack.cmd` present and asserts Corepack steps are selected.
4. Optionally document that `corepack prepare` alone may not put `pnpm` on PATH on Windows — Corepack invoke remains the supported path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On Windows native without `sh` on PATH, with `corepack.cmd` present and no bare `pnpm`, `task build` / `engine:_ts-build` attempts Corepack instead of exit 127 "neither pnpm nor corepack"
- [ ] `hasCmd('corepack')` (or equivalent) is true when `Get-Command corepack` would succeed in PowerShell
- [ ] False-negative remediation ("enable Corepack") is not printed when Corepack is already available
- [ ] Linux/macOS path still works (bare pnpm and Corepack)
- [ ] Regression test covers Windows-shaped PATH (no `sh`, `.cmd` shim present)

## Non-goals

- Requiring a global `pnpm` install on Windows
- Reverting #2410 Corepack resolution
- Changing session/runtime global fallback (#2409)

## Related

- Refs #2410 (closed/incomplete on Windows native detection)
- Refs #2411 (shipped Corepack resolver that introduced this probe)
- Sibling verified fixed on same host: #2409 (`task session:start`), #2367 (`deft policy:show` after 0.73.1)
- Adjacent Windows Taskfile path work: #2120 (closed)

## Labels

`bug`, `adoption-blocker`
narratives.UserStory: As a Windows-native maintainer without Unix sh on PATH, I want engine:_ts-build to detect Corepack via .cmd shims, so that task build and policy verbs work when bare pnpm is absent.

items.title: Windows without sh still selects Corepack

narrative.Acceptance: Given Windows native PATH with corepack.cmd present, no bare pnpm, and no sh, when engine:_ts-build / pm-run runs, then Corepack steps are queued instead of exit 127 claiming neither pnpm nor corepack.

items.title: hasCmd true when PowerShell Get-Command would succeed

narrative.Acceptance: Given corepack is resolvable as a .cmd shim, when hasCmd('corepack') runs, then it returns true without requiring Unix sh.

items.title: False remediation not printed when Corepack present

narrative.Acceptance: Given Corepack is available, when the resolver runs, then it does not print the enable-Corepack remediation as if Corepack were missing.
Given Linux/macOS with bare pnpm or Corepack, when build runs, then the #2411 step order still applies; session/runtime verbs still do not auto-build (#2181).
Given content-contract tests, when they run, then they assert hasCmd does not rely solely on sh/command -v and covers the cross-platform probe.
